summary: @ornikar/eslint-config preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated bundled payload
details: The package declares scripts.preinstall = "node setup.mjs". setup.mjs is obfuscated (obfuscator.io-style hex identifiers and string-map lookups) and, on install, downloads the Bun runtime from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/<platform>.zip to a temp directory, chmods it executable, and uses it (execFileSync) to run the sibling file math_init.js — a 727KB single-line obfuscated Bun-compiled bundle beginning with `// @bun @bun-cjs` and containing a shuffled numeric constant array with a shift-based decode routine. An ESLint configuration package has no legitimate need to fetch a second language runtime at install time or to execute an opaque compiled bundle with it. The runtime fetch itself is from Bun's official GitHub releases, but the harmful action is that the fetched runtime is used to execute attacker-supplied, obfuscated in-tarball code that is unrelated to the package's declared purpose; the alternate runtime is used to evade Node-based static analysis of the executed payload. This fires automatically on `npm install` via the preinstall lifecycle hook.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
